$comment: Canonical map of every surface this test app contributes to a Horizon host: SDK zone extensions, full-page routes, and one dynamic table column. Single source of truth shared by the app (src/integration/zones.js drives registration from it) and the netsapiens-horizon-testing Playwright suite (asserts each testId mounts). testId scheme: extensions 'sdk-testapp-ext-<id minus the app prefix>', routes 'sdk-testapp-page-<slug>', columns 'sdk-testapp-col-<field>'. ⚠ 'render' names which registration path each extension takes, and they are mutually exclusive: 'component' means the app draws it and the marker (data-testid + data-zone) rides on the widget's OWN root element; 'actions' means the app DECLARES a button and the HOST draws it in the house style (SDK 0.2.6), so only data-testid is emitted — there is no data-zone on those three. The host rejects and logs a registration carrying both or neither. Either way assert VISIBILITY (toBeVisible) on the testId; a component that renders null (an inactive zone) has no marker, which is the accurate signal. 'requiredScopes' is a NARROWING request, never a grant — the host intersects it with the gate of the page, so it cannot reveal anything a user could not already reach. 'version' mirrors package.json and is the value to register the app under: the remote entry URL is stable, so the registered version is the only thing that tells Horizon to re-verify the bytes at that URL.
$zoneCoverage: All 12 INJECTABLE zones in the host catalogue (SDKSettings.tsx ZONE_CATALOGUE). The other 5 catalogue entries are Navigation zones, which are not injection points — they gate which nav sections an app may add PAGES to, and are covered by 'routes' below. nav-marketplace is reserved to the built-in marketplace and can never be covered by a third-party app.

extensions.label: Side-tray section
extensions.$note: Not covered by horizon-sdk-demo — this zone had no test coverage before the testapp cutover.

extensions.label: Inbound-call content card
extensions.$state: Requires a live ringing call to render — the suite marks this fixme rather than faking call state.

columns.$note: The host's DataTable derives the `call-logs-columns` zone from the route and merges registered columns into the grid. `table-columns` is the catalogue's name for the capability; `call-logs-columns` is the concrete zone id the host emits for this page.

$scopeNote: Only the /manage and /platform routes declare requiredScopes, and they declare the tier those sections already floor at (ADMINS). That is deliberate: it exercises the 0.2.4 scope-declaration contract end to end while remaining a no-op in effect, so the suite's outcome does not depend on which scope it authenticates as. Declaring something NARROWER than the page floor (e.g. PLATFORM on an ADMINS page) would be a stronger test of intersection but would silently start failing if this suite is ever run as a Reseller.
